_source: day3/design/validation-rules-hassan.md (Lab 2 paper design). Rule ids match the paper design. Rule types: day3/rules/RULE_TYPES.md.

file_rules.why: A renamed or missing column breaks every rule after it: reject the whole file.

rules.why: Nothing to settle or trace without them; every column feeds a later rule.
A PNR of the wrong length or case can't be matched to the booking.
IATA designators are 2 characters (digits allowed, e.g. 6E).
We only settle carriers we have a contract and ticket prefix for.
One upper-case letter; never silently upper-case a money-driving field.
An unpublished class has no fare rules, so no refund or commission basis.
Origin and destination must be split reliably: AAA-BBB.
An unknown airport can't be priced or reported by route.
Same origin and destination is well-formed but not a journey.
INR is 2 dp; more means upstream rounding is broken, and we never round for them.
A ticket-issue file can't carry a zero or negative fare; refunds come through a different feed.
An unknown currency code silently mis-converts the settlement.
3-digit airline prefix, hyphen, 10 digits, or it can't be matched to BSP sales.
A ticket prefix of another airline would be settled against the wrong carrier.
Only ISO dates; we don't guess between DD/MM and MM/DD.
A ticket can't be issued after the file that reports it was cut.
A valid sale reported late is still owed: settle it, but flag it for ops.
The agency owes the remittance; a malformed agency code can't be billed.
Same ticket twice in one file: keep the first, skip and count the repeat.
Custom: separates a wrong-shape currency from an unknown code (R-12) in the quarantine folders.
